preconditions: The anlmdn filter is applied (ffmpeg -af anlmdn, or a libavfilter graph using the filter)
The input audio stream length (in samples) is not a multiple of the filter block size H = 2K+1 (default patch=2000us; at 44100 Hz K=88, H=177), so the final frame is short
No special privilege is required: processing a crafted WAV/audio file is sufficient

evidence.vulnerable_version: FFmpeg <= n9.0.2 and <= n8.1.3 (latest releases as of 2026-11); the vulnerable loop `for (int i = S; i < H + S; i++)` is present since the filter was added (2019, FFmpeg 4.2)
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased on master (2e70a189, 2026-11-06); NOT in any release branch as of 2026-11-15
evidence.observed_result: Driving the REAL FFmpeg 9.0.2 binary (compiled from source with musl-gcc, allocator instrumented with a canary redzone because ASAN is unavailable): a 178-sample 44.1kHz WAV (H+1, final frame = 1 sample) processed through `-af anlmdn` triggers `AIVR-CANARY: HEAP-BUFFER-OVERFLOW detected in av_malloc buffer (size=136 bytes): redzone byte 0 == 0x00 (expected 0xa5)` and aborts (exit 134/SIGABRT). CONTROL (177-sample WAV, multiple of H) exits 0. The FIXED binary (one-line loop-bound change) processes the same 178-sample input with exit 0, proving the overflow is the vulnerable loop. Marker: FFMPEGOVERRUN-OK.

real_exploit.target: FFmpeg 9.0.2 (the real libavfilter/af_anlmdn.c filter_channel loop), compiled from upstream source at tag n9.0.2 with musl-gcc; the vulnerable code is byte-for-byte upstream, only av_malloc is instrumented with a canary redzone for deterministic OOB-write detection
real_exploit.backend: the real ffmpeg binary (ffmpeg-vuln) decoding a crafted WAV and running the anlmdn filter; gen_wav.py crafts the 178-sample (H+1) input whose final 1-sample frame overflows by 704 bytes
real_exploit.demonstrated: ffmpeg-vuln (n9.0.2) aborts with the canary marker on the 178-sample input (short final frame -> 704-byte out-of-bounds write past a 4-byte float buffer), while the 177-sample control exits cleanly; ffmpeg-fixed (same source + the one-line `i < in->nb_samples + S` fix) processes the identical 178-sample input with exit 0. Demonstrated impact = deterministic heap corruption / process abort (DoS, A:H); the write is bounded and carries denoised float data, so I:H is NOT claimed (honest MEDIUM 5.5, C:N/I:N/A:H).

evidence.notes: No CVE assigned as of 2026-11-15; upstream tracks it under FFmpeg ticket uQUc1sfqWcj8, reported by Secbuddy / Tencent Keen Security Lab and fixed by Michael Niedermayer on 2026-11-06. The fix commit message states 'Fixes: heap-buffer-overflow' and 'Heap out of array write Replicated through UnModified FFmpeg with ASAN'. Fix is on master only; the n9.0.2 and n8.1.3 release branches still carry the vulnerable loop.
